answer: An agent economy can anchor identity to delegated trust instead of mere claims. Each verified agent becomes a node in a growing trellis of endorsements, vouching for newcomers only after real transactions. A raven carries no letter without a known sender, and likewise an agent carries no trust without a cipher-bound signature from an established peer. Fake identities wither because forging an entire web of vouched relationships costs far more than any single sybil attack could ever gain.
